failedChecks: Item 1 (SEC-R17-3, the checklist's explicit 'implement this before anything else' control): NOT EVIDENCED. The packet contains no code for submit's pre-send duplicate-evidence check, no exit-6 path, and no proof it consults unresolvedDuplicateEntries()/unresolvedDirectEvidence(). The only submit-adjacent code supplied is youngestMarkerAgeMs(), which implements a *time-based* gate; a gate that clears by waiting is not the gate the checklist specified (which requires `resolve` first, exit 6). Unverifiable from packet, and it is the highest-priority item.

Round-1 fix #4 (credential TOCTOU): INCOMPLETE EVIDENCE, possible unfixed race. validateCredentialFileHandle is correctly fd-bound on linux/darwin, but the actual content read is elided as '// ... read + UTF-8 decode + JSON.parse ... unchanged from round 1'. If the round-1 read was path-based (fsp.readFile(source.path)), the validation is fd-bound while the read is not, and the race is moved rather than closed. This is precisely the question the task asked to check, and the packet redacts the deciding line.

Item 4 (late direct evidence): PARTIALLY RESOLVED. The discarded-state path and the unresolvedDirectEvidence() candidate source do work as claimed (no revival; audit-only annotation via discardedDraftEvidenceOnly). But the `--distinct` dismissal branch is elided ('// ... dismissal path, guards submitted/unknown-without-evidence states'), and that branch calls queueAudit('duplicate-dismissed', { dismissedKeys: candidates }) — dismissing ALL candidates wholesale, including direct evidence of our own successful POST. Whether `resolve --distinct` can clear the very marker item 1's submit gate depends on cannot be determined from the packet.

Item 7 (verify-clear evidentiary standard) / round-1 fix #3: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. verifyClearMinimumAgeMs derives from state.poll.minimumDurationMs with a 30s floor, which is defensible as a floor but is a proxy for poll duration, not an index-lag bound — the original objection was specifically the absence of an index-lag budget. Worse, boundedSearch does not enforce probe *spacing*: when minimumDurationMs has already elapsed on a slow first probe, the sleep collapses to Math.max(1, ceil(0/n)) = 1ms, so the remaining minimum probes fire back-to-back within milliseconds. 'minimumProbes=3 + minimumDurationMs elapsed' is therefore satisfiable by a burst that adds no independent index-lag evidence — the exact weakness Opus raised at round 17.

boundedSearch return-shape conflation (new, packet-visible): a truncated/deadline-exhausted poll and a genuinely completed zero-match both return { kind: 'matches', keys: [] }, differing only in a `complete` boolean. A network error at/after the deadline is also converted into kind:'matches', keys:[], complete:false. Every zero-match → approved / verify-clear inference in the design therefore depends on every caller remembering to test `complete`; the type does not fail closed. No caller code was supplied, so this cannot be checked.

Item 11 (submit --dry-run exit list): PARTIALLY ADDRESSED. Exits 1 and 13 are now claimed documented (with a regression test for 13), and round 1's CONFIG_INVALID claim is correctly retracted. But the original round-17 objection was that dry-run holds the lock and runs the fence check, making 16/17/18/19 reachable; the packet says nothing about those four codes. Their documented status is unverified.

Items 2 (posted:false vs 429-backoff recovery mislabel), 3 (attempts[].outcome model / aborted-before-post not in §2), 5 (trigger (e) coverage for a late-indexing 429-created issue), 6 (unfreeze clearing canonicalPayload/payloadSha256/configFingerprint/approvedAt), 9 (normative fetch-error → failure-class mapping), 10 (unnumbered 'existing state-error code' row in the authoritative exit inventory), 13 (smoke-test pinning of POST /rest/api/3/search/jql and its cursor pagination), 15 (crash-recovery mixing trigger-(d) verify semantics with §7 reconcile semantics): NO EVIDENCE SUPPLIED. Genuinely unverifiable from this packet — not a guess, an absence.

Item 14 (maxAttempts total-vs-retry ambiguity): UNVERIFIABLE, and the packet is internally inconsistent about it. The task states 'item 14 ... which you now have verbatim', and round-1 disposition #3 refers to a '§7 index-lag/bounded-poll model (verbatim excerpt below)'. Neither the §7 excerpt nor any maxAttempts spec text or implementation appears anywhere in the packet. boundedSearch exposes minimum/maximumProbes (poll probes), which is a different quantity from maxAttempts (POST attempts).

None of the six claimed new tests — malformed-timestamp blocking, the 29999/30000 injected-clock boundary, descriptor-bound path-swap rejection, doctor accountId fallback, case-insensitive email match, dry-run exit-13 regression — is individually visible. The only evidence is that boundedSearch calls visibilityPrecheck() and returns a distinct kind:'visibility-failed' — good structure, but the precheck's contents are not shown, and the finding was never about structure: project-default issue-security schemes and workflow/automation post-functions bypass defaultFields entirely.

Item 18 (attacker-controlled *.atlassian.net tenant) is not merely unresolved — round-1 fix #5 weakened its proposed mitigation. The suggested doctor-time control was 'check /rest/api/3/myself returns the configured resolvedEmail'; the fix makes a missing emailAddress warn and fall back to accountId, which is the *default* Jira Cloud posture. securityFindings.summary: Credential TOCTOU fix may be incomplete: identity/containment validation is now bound to the open file descriptor (correct on linux/darwin via /proc/self/fd and /dev/fd), but the code that actually reads the credential bytes is elided as 'unchanged from round 1'. If that read is still path-based rather than handle-based, an attacker who can swap the path retains the original race and the validation is decorative. Cannot be resolved from the packet; requires showing the read call.

External side effects are gated only by prose. All five SKILL.md diffs restrict kstack-jira to the offline `draft` command and explicitly state that authority.externalTicketCreation is 'a calling-skill convention, not an enforced CLI boundary'. Nothing in kstack-jira.mjs enforces it, so any agent, script, or skill lacking that paragraph can invoke `submit` and create a real Jira issue. The diffs do not weaken any gate, but they document that the only control over the one command with an irreversible external side effect is unenforced. Recommend a CLI-level check of authority.externalTicketCreation on submit/approve.

`resolve --distinct` may be able to dismiss the duplicate evidence the submit gate depends on. The visible code passes the full `candidates` array — which includes unresolvedDirectEvidence() keys, i.e. evidence that this queue's own POST already created an issue — to queueAudit('duplicate-dismissed', { dismissedKeys: candidates }). If the elided guards do not specifically refuse to dismiss direct (non-search-derived) evidence, `--distinct` becomes a one-command bypass of the SEC-R17-3 control, re-enabling the double-POST it was added to prevent.

Credential protections silently degrade to no-ops off linux/darwin. descriptorRealpath falls back to realpath(path) + dev/ino comparison, but Node reports ino as 0/unstable on win32, making the identity check vacuous; O_NOFOLLOW resolves to 0; process.getuid is undefined so the ownership check is skipped; and (stat.mode & 0o077) is meaningless on Windows. The result is a platform where every credential safety check passes trivially, with no warning. (Raised as new to this round's fix, distinct from the deferred QC-SEC-5 O_NOFOLLOW warning.)

Open-before-classify introduces a hang: resolveCredentials opens source.path with O_RDONLY and no O_NONBLOCK, and only afterwards checks descriptorStat.isFile(). If the configured path is a FIFO, the open blocks indefinitely waiting for a writer, before any validation runs. The prior lstat-first ordering would have rejected it. Low severity (requires control of the configured path) but it is a regression created by this round's reordering.

Unsafe-direction conflation in boundedSearch: deadline-truncated polls and post-deadline network errors are both returned as kind:'matches' with keys:[] and complete:false — structurally identical to a verified zero-match. Since every 'unknown → approved' and verify-clear inference in the design rests on zero-match, a single caller that omits the `complete` check turns an inconclusive or failed search into affirmative evidence that no issue exists. A distinct kind ('inconclusive') would fail closed by construction.

materialDissent: I dissent from treating round-1 disposition #3 as resolved. Deriving the minimum age from poll.minimumDurationMs makes the constant configuration-linked, not spec-derived in the sense the objection required: minimumDurationMs bounds how long one poll ran, and is not an index-lag bound. Combined with the 1ms floor sleep in boundedSearch, the 'minimum probes + minimum duration' evidentiary standard remains satisfiable by a burst of near-simultaneous probes. Item 7 is partially, not fully, resolved.

I dissent from any reading that item 4 is fully closed. The discarded-state path is correctly implemented and does not revive the draft, but the acknowledged key is recorded only in the audit trail — draft.result is never populated for a discarded draft — so any consumer that reads result.key will not see the acknowledged duplicate. Whether `status` surfaces the audit annotation is not shown.

I dissent from accepting the remediation as verified on the strength of the npm test output. Nine passing suite files is compatible with all six claimed new tests being absent or asserting something weaker than described. Per-test output (node --test-reporter=spec) or the test source is required before the NaN-fail-open and descriptor-binding fixes can be called verified rather than claimed.

I do NOT dissent on boundedSearch's use of raw Date.now(). It is loop-internal wall-clock timing against a live network deadline, not a comparison against persisted state; an injected clock there would make a real-time bound untestable against reality. This is a different defect class from the fixed youngestMarkerAgeMs bug, and I agree it should not be flagged.

I do NOT find gate weakening in the five SKILL.md diffs. Each narrows the callable surface to the offline `draft` command and explicitly forbids approve/submit/network commands; kstack-review's phrasing is the strongest and the others are equivalent. The concern is the unenforced-authority disclosure (OPUS-R2-SEC-2), not weakening.

Round-1 fixes #1 and #2 are correct as written and I confirm them on the code shown. youngestMarkerAgeMs fails closed on every non-finite input (non-finite now, any non-finite marker timestamp, non-finite difference), uses the injected clock, and returns a negative (therefore blocking) age under future-dated clock skew. Infinity for an empty marker set is the correct identity. The only caveat is that the comparison operator at the call site is not shown, so the claimed 29999-blocks/30000-clears boundary cannot be confirmed independently.
review.strongestObjection: The packet's elisions land exactly on the load-bearing lines. Three of the four most consequential items are decided by code that was redacted or never supplied: (a) item 1, the checklist's own 'implement this before anything else' control-bypass fix, appears nowhere in the packet — the only submit-adjacent code shown is a time-based age gate that clears by waiting, which is not the specified 'requires resolve first, exit 6' control; (b) the credential-TOCTOU fix is validated fd-bound but the actual read is elided as 'unchanged from round 1', which is precisely the difference between closing the race and relocating it; (c) resolve's `--distinct` dismissal branch is elided while the visible code hands it the full candidate list including direct POST evidence — the one path that could unwind item 1's control. Round 1 was told its 'unverifiable' verdicts came from an incomplete packet; this packet is much better, but on the specific items that matter most it reproduces the same defect, and I cannot certify a control I have never seen.
unresolvedQuestions: Show submit's pre-send duplicate-evidence check verbatim: the predicate, its evidence sources (unresolvedDuplicateEntries and unresolvedDirectEvidence), the exit code (must be 6), and confirmation that it is not satisfiable by elapsed time alone.
Show the elided credential read. Is it handle.readFile()/read-from-fd, or fsp.readFile(source.path)? This single line determines whether round-1 fix #4 is real.
Show the elided `resolve --distinct` guard block. Can it dismiss direct evidence (a folded posted:true+key sidecar), or only search-derived reconcile-matches keys?
Supply the §7 verbatim excerpt and the maxAttempts spec text and implementation. Both were stated to be in this packet and are not; item 14 cannot be assessed without them.
Do all callers of boundedSearch test `complete` before drawing a zero-match inference? Show the call sites for approve/reconcile/verify-clear/doctor.
Are exits 16/17/18/19 now in submit --dry-run's documented exit list, given that dry-run holds the lock and runs the fence check?
What configured value does doctor compare accountId against when /myself omits emailAddress, and does the accountId fallback still detect a wrong-tenant credential (item 18)?
Do status/reconcile surface sweepQueue's non-empty held[] and errors[], and does a non-empty errors[] affect the process exit code — or are janitor failures silently swallowed during a sweep?

Per-test output or the source of tests/jira-queue.test.mjs, to confirm the six claimed new tests exist and assert what is claimed (particularly the 29999/30000 boundary and the post-open path-swap rejection).

Is poll configuration validated (minimumProbes <= maximumProbes, minimumDurationMs <= maximumDurationMs)? Inverted bounds make complete:true unreachable — fail-closed, but silently and permanently inconclusive.

Is there any intended CLI-level enforcement point for authority.externalTicketCreation, or is prose-in-SKILL.md the accepted final control for the one command with an irreversible external side effect?
review.recommendation: Revise — one more targeted round, then this is close. The remediation is real and the code that was shown is largely well-constructed: fixes #1 (NaN fail-open), #2 (injected clock), and #5 (doctor email fallback) are correct on the evidence; item 12 (sweep skip-and-continue with held[]/errors[]) is confirmed resolved; item 4 is resolved for the discarded and unknown sub-cases; fix #4 closes the containment race on linux/darwin; and the five SKILL.md diffs narrow rather than weaken the callable surface. Do not block. But do not approve either: of the 19 checklist items I can confirm 3 resolved (4-partial, 12, plus round-1 fixes 1/2/5/6), 4 partially resolved (1-unevidenced, 7, 11, 8/16-structural), and 9 are genuinely unverifiable from this packet with no code or spec text supplied. Required before round 3: (1) supply submit's pre-send duplicate gate — item 1 is the checklist's stated first priority and is the only item the design called a control bypass; (2) supply the credential read line and, if path-based, convert it to a read from the open handle; (3) supply the `--distinct` guard block and, if it can dismiss direct evidence, prohibit that; (4) supply the §7 and maxAttempts spec text promised but absent; (5) supply per-test output or the test source; (6) either enforce probe spacing in boundedSearch or explicitly record that the min-probe requirement is burst-satisfiable and that item 7 remains open by decision; (7) give truncated/errored polls a distinct return kind so zero-match inference fails closed by construction; (8) decide whether authority.externalTicketCreation gets a CLI check or is accepted as prose-only residual risk. Items 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 13, 15 need evidence packaged, not necessarily new work — several may already be implemented. On the two explicitly out-of-scope items I concur: exit-code numbering vs Node reserved codes and the directory-permission/O_NOFOLLOW degradation are correctly deferred, though OPUS-R2-SEC-4 (win32 checks degrading to vacuous, not just O_NOFOLLOW) is new to this round's fix and should be logged rather than folded into the deferred item.
